sections.label: Material facts
sections.summary: The author was detained on 25 November 1989, allegedly without a warrant until 29 November, denied legal assistance until 6 December, subjected to 48 hours of interrogation without food or sleep, and later sentenced to death (commuted to life imprisonment). The trial environment was hostile, with media prejudice and intimidation of witnesses and defence counsel.

The facts as submitted by the author
2. The author was arrested on 25 November 1989 on charges of
attempted rape and murder of one Ms. Zykina. Once in detention, he was
also charged with six other assaults. On 3 October 1990, the Chelyabinsk
Regional Court found him guilty of the charges and sentenced him to
death. His appeal to the Supreme Court was rejected on 21 June 1991.
Further appeals were rejected on 21 October 1991 and 1 July 1992.
Appeals to the Prosecutor's Office were likewise rejected, respectively
on 12 December 1991, 16 January and 11 March 1992. On 3 December 1993,
the author's death sentence was commuted to life imprisonment.
The complaint

sections.label: Issue and actual outcome
sections.summary: The author alleged violations of article 14(1) (fair trial) and article 14(2) (presumption of innocence). The Committee concluded that the State violated article 14(2) by failing to restrain public officials from prejudicing the trial, but found no violation of article 14(1) regarding the overall fairness of the proceedings.

8.3 With regard to the allegation of a violation of the presumption of
innocence, including public statements made by high ranking law
enforcement officials portraying the author as guilty which were given
wide media coverage, the Committee notes that the Supreme Court referred
to the issue, but failed to specifically deal with it when it heard the
author’s appeal. The Committee refers to its General Comment No 13 on
article 14, where it has stated that: “It is, therefore, a duty for all
public authorities to refrain from prejudging the outcome of a trial”.
In the present case the Committee considers that the authorities failed
to exercise the restraint that article 14, paragraph 2, requires of them
and that the author’s rights were thus violated.

sections.label: Deciding body's reasoning
sections.summary: The Committee applied General Comment No. 13 on article 14, emphasizing the duty of authorities to refrain from prejudging outcomes. It noted that high‑ranking officials publicly declared the author guilty, which breached the restraint required by article 14(2). The lack of specific address of the presumption‑of‑innocence claim by the Supreme Court was highlighted as insufficient.

sections.summary: The Committee reminded the State of its obligations under article 2 of the Covenant to provide effective remedies and to report measures taken within 90 days, reflecting the standard procedural follow‑up required in CCPR cases.
